title: Objectwise bijectivity of graph evaluation
statement: Let $V$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $P$ a finite group, $c:Y\to V$ an $\operatorname{ULift}(P)$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], $\ell\in\mathbb N$, and $N$ a $\mathbb Z/\ell$-representation of $P$. For every etale object $W\to Y$, let $d_W:W\to W\times_V Y$ be its graph. Evaluation $s\mapsto s\circ d_W$ is a bijection from the equivariant locally constant sections [def-weil-pbc-torsor-associated-module] over $W\to V$ to locally constant functions $W\to N$. Both sides may be regarded as modules over $\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbb Z/\ell)$ by restriction of scalars.

proof.text: Reindex the torsor coproduct from ULift(P) to P using Sigma.reindex, and interchange the two pullback factors. The result is the isomorphism with components (identity, g-action). Apply the already proved library lemma CategoryTheory.FinitaryPreExtensive.isIso_sigmaDesc_lift_comp to W.hom. Pullback projection identities identify the resulting coproduct components with the translates of the graph.

Compose AlgebraicGeometry.sigmaMk with the homeomorphism of this scheme isomorphism. This gives a homeomorphism E from the disjoint union of copies of W indexed by P to the section space, with E(g,w)=g times d_W(w). The torsor action identities imply h times E(g,w)=E(hg,w).

Injectivity: write each point as E(g,w) using surjectivity of the homeomorphism. Equivariance determines a section there as rho(g) applied to its value on the graph. Equal graph restrictions therefore give equal sections.

Surjectivity: give N the discrete topology, and on the disjoint union define f(g,w)=rho(g)t(w). Each restriction is continuous, so continuous_sigma proves continuity of f, hence local constancy. Compose with E inverse. The action identity and rho(hg)=rho(h)rho(g) give equivariance, while rho(1)=identity proves graph restriction equals t. Empty W and zero modules require no choices or separate assumptions.
